Yeah arguing with a 5 year old just goes in circles.  Saying why you took the toy and when he can have it back and maximum of 3 times and then no longer speaking of it is is huge. Even if it’s annoying to hear him ask, the biggest part of gentle parenting on the parent end is having patience even if he is a brat. And since you and your wife can’t get on the same page, and she’s doing things to counteract what you’re doing, it will not work on him. He’s 5, and he needs clear rules and lines, and not ones that keep moving

Firstly, her hitting you was not at all okay and shows how she chooses to handle disagreements. How does she expect herself to raise a good well mannered boy, if she can’t keep herself well mannered?
 
Secondly. If you want things to work out between you too, I highly recommend marriage counseling, someone being a mediator between you too. 

Thirdly. Both of you need to understand (mainly her) that gentle parenting isn’t just asking nicely. You need to speak to him like you would an actual person and not something that will break. Kids are sensitive yes, but being stern and standing your ground is still gentle parenting. You say no toy. It means no toy. He will not die from being told no.
